sources.title: Hazardous substances consent
sources.verified_claim: Hazardous substances at or above controlled quantities require consent from the hazardous substances authority; HSE is a statutory consultee and produces risk-zone advice.

sources.title: Hazardous Substance Consent Application FAQ
sources.verified_claim: The HSE wizard helps prepare consent, variation or continuation forms but is not itself an online submission service to the planning authority.

sources.title: Why is HSE involved?
sources.verified_claim: Decision-makers must consult HSE on certain proposals around major-hazard establishments and pipelines and consider HSE advice.

sources.title: HSE land use planning methodology
sources.verified_claim: HSE uses consultation distances and its Planning Advice Web App to provide advise-against or do-not-advise-against safety advice.

sources.title: HSE Planning Advice Web App
sources.verified_claim: Developers can check whether a proposal lies within a major-hazard consultation distance; proposal-specific pre-application advice is separate and exact location dependent.

sources.title: Current land use planning legislation
sources.verified_claim: HSE lists the planning and hazardous-substances legislation governing consultation and consent in England.

sources.title: Hazardous substances planning guidance
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Hazardous-substances consent controls specified quantities and is distinct from planning permission and, where relevant, environmental permitting.

sources.title: Control Of Major Accident Hazards Regulations 2015
sources.verified_claim: COMAH regulates major-accident hazards while land-use planning requirements are implemented through planning legislation; the regimes must not be conflated.
